title: Not my account
guidance: Consumer says they never opened this account. Common after identity mix-ups, similar names, or reporting errors. Furnisher must confirm the account actually belongs to this consumer using identifying information on file; if ownership can't be confirmed, the tradeline should be corrected or removed.
keywords: not mine never opened this account do not recognize unauthorized someone else's account not my account

title: Incorrect balance
guidance: Consumer disputes the reported balance amount. Usually a timing gap between a payment posting and the furnisher's next report, or a processing error on the furnisher's side. Furnisher should verify the balance as of the report date against their own ledger.
keywords: balance is wrong incorrect balance amount too high wrong amount owed balance shown is wrong

title: Incorrect payment history
guidance: Consumer disputes one or more reported late or missed payments. Often caused by payment-posting delays, address changes that misrouted a statement, or a furnisher system error. Furnisher must re-check the payment ledger month by month against what was reported.
keywords: late payment marked wrong never missed a payment always paid on time incorrect late marks payment history wrong

title: Account status incorrect (open/closed)
guidance: Consumer says an account is reported as open when it was closed (or vice versa). Common when a closure request wasn't processed downstream to the bureau feed. Furnisher should confirm current account status and correct the reported status if it's stale.
keywords: account shows open but is closed account shows closed but still open wrong account status

title: Duplicate account reported
guidance: The same underlying account appears more than once on the report, often after a balance transfer, account renumbering, or a furnisher system migration. Furnisher should identify which tradeline is current and request removal of the duplicate.
keywords: duplicate account same account listed twice appears twice on my report duplicate tradeline

title: Incorrect date opened
guidance: Consumer disputes the reported account-opening date, which affects how the account factors into credit age. Frequently caused by confusing an account renewal or reissue date with the true origination date. Furnisher should confirm the original opening date from account records.
keywords: wrong date account opened incorrect open date account age is wrong opening date wrong

title: Paid in full but showing balance due
guidance: Consumer paid off the account but it still reports an outstanding balance. Usually a lag between the payoff transaction and the furnisher's next reporting cycle, though it can also indicate a misapplied payment. Furnisher should confirm the payoff posted correctly.
keywords: already paid off paid in full balance should be zero payoff not reflected still shows balance due

title: Suspected identity theft / fraud
guidance: Consumer states the account was opened fraudulently and not by them. This is treated as higher-risk and time-sensitive; it typically involves fraud-alert or identity-theft procedures beyond a standard reinvestigation, and is generally routed for extra verification rather than auto-processed.
keywords: identity theft fraud someone stole my identity fraudulent account not authorized by me scam account opened without permission

title: Incorrect credit limit / high balance
guidance: Consumer disputes the reported credit limit or high-balance figure, which affects credit utilization calculations. Often the limit was changed (increased or decreased) but the change wasn't reflected in the furnisher's next report. Furnisher should confirm the current limit on file.
keywords: credit limit is wrong incorrect limit wrong high balance limit not updated wrong credit limit reported

title: Account should be removed after bankruptcy discharge
guidance: Consumer says an account included in a bankruptcy discharge is still reporting a balance or delinquency status after discharge. This has specific post-discharge reporting requirements; furnisher must update the account to reflect discharged status rather than continuing to report it as owed.
keywords: bankruptcy discharged should not show balance after bankruptcy discharge account still reporting owed after discharge
